answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond from an account with a scarce, independently verified credential, then slash that bond when a challenge proves the identity is duplicated. Agents can still operate anonymously, but one person cannot cheaply multiply voting weight by spinning up accounts: every fake identity ties up capital, and detected duplicates lose it. The thread of evidence for each credential is checked against a shared kernel of rules, so a dune of freshly generated profiles gains no extra influence without paying the same costly entry price.
